neutral_facts.value: The prosecution case was that the accused conspired to misappropriate bags of fertilizers and made false entries in the records. An initial complaint was lodged alleging misappropriation of 540 bags of urea, but an investigation revealed that the entire 1040 bags of urea were misappropriated. The accused were responsible for falsifying records to show that the fertilizers were delivered to the FCI godown, despite no actual delivery. The prosecution presented documentary and oral evidence, including entries in registers and statements from witnesses, to prove the conspiracy and falsification of accounts. The trial court convicted the accused, and the High Court confirmed the conviction but reduced the sentence. The Supreme Court upheld the conviction, noting that the evidence proved the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.

quotes.text: High Court confirmed the conviction

Dismissing the appeals, the Court HELD: 1. At the outset, it is to be noted that the initial complaint was lodged alleging misappropriation of only 540 bags of urea but investigation revealed that entire 1040 bags of urea was misappropriated.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the appellants conspired and misappropriated 1040 bags of urea, falsifying records to show delivery at FCI godown at Tilrath, despite no actual delivery.

quotes.text: It is the specific allegation of the prosecution that the appellants and other accused have conspired with criminal intent and indulged in the falsification of accounts.

Out of 1040 bags of urea, 500 bags were shown to have loaded in the trucks bearing nos.BRI-7851 and BHF-3155 with 250 bags each for delivering the same at F.C.I. godown at Tilrath but it was found that there was no actual delivery of such fertiliser bags and the F.C.I. records were falsified.

defence_argument.value: The defence contended that the prosecution failed to prove misappropriation of 1040 bags, relying on inconsistent evidence and that the FIR was based on only 540 bags, not 1040.

quotes.text: It is contended that though, the prosecution has mainly relied on the evidence of PW-9, PW-10 and PW-14, truck driver, Khalasi(cleaner) and owner respectively of truck bearing no.BHF-3155, PW-15 and PW-18, the owner and the driver respectively of truck bearing no. BRI-7851, in arriving at the conclusion that 50,00 bags were not delivered at Tilrath godown, but on a fair perusal of the evidence of the said witnesses, there were several inconsistencies and contradictions.
It is submitted that the FIR was lodged with regard to only 540 bags but not with regard to 1040 bags of urea, as alleged by the prosecution.

legal_principle_applied.value: The court applied the principle that the prosecution must prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt, considering the totality of oral and documentary evidence.

quotes.text: Considering the totality of oral and documentary evidence on record, the prosecution has proved the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.

Having regard to evidence on record, it cannot be said that findings recorded by the trial court, as affirmed by the appellate court, are either perverse or erroneous so as to interfere with the same.

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed because the prosecution proved the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt, and the courts found the findings of the trial and appellate courts to be correct.
